## Result and decision still open

The first unpenalized MDEA start converged in **9 optimizer iterations** at
weighted fitted cost **382.06387056074306**. The previous B1 fit gives
**374.51907880524016** on the same 278 fitted observations and residual definitions.
The first F2 endpoint therefore has a higher fitted cost. It is not a selected
parameter record: its full stability search is running, and the second start
has not yet been fitted. No parameter record is adopted.

These results are calibration, comparisons on previously accessed data, and
numerical verification. They do not establish independent physical validation,
parameter identification, or suitability for absorber design. No agreement
threshold is imposed. The finite search can supply only a lower bound on splits;
unavailable searches will remain unavailable, never counted as stable.

The [paper summary](results/stage-b-start-0-report/paper-summary.json),
[parameter values](results/stage-b-start-0-report/parameter-values.csv), and
[curve data](results/stage-b-start-0-report/curve-data.json) retain the currently
completed endpoint. Their unselected status must accompany any use.
The previous notebook, including Stage A qualification and the historical B1
study, remains in [the pre-campaign Git record](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/blob/2e5b2d413fe8177ac27a7a1cf4a546bf674a4d1f/analyses/mdea_mea_workflow/notebook.qmd).

## Model, inputs and data roles

The calculation uses one F2 shared-value record and one Engine wheel:

- F2: `part-ii-shared-values.json`, SHA-256
  `4c27d47ea7b6e018b0603efb8a29fc2f3fe3c6f8fdc12ccc12cb10bb4b315334`.
- Engine commit `391dfe5d`, wheel SHA-256
  `0962e21d2fa7a8ba1ed4622f1110b3e8053bacd878fa41c999d85e8b9afab66b`.

The shared R1–R3 laws and water–bicarbonate interaction
**0.7650000233694618** follow F2; water–carbonate is **−0.25**.
The protonated-MDEA Born diameter is tied to its segment diameter, removing the
historical independently fitted Born diameter at 7 Å. The eight remaining
coordinates, scales and bounds retain their declared owners. Fixed shared
inputs have no fitted standard error.

The [immutable campaign declaration](inputs/stage-b.json) binds the complete
starts, species specification, data roles, source ranges, grid and MDEA split
record by hash. The one calculation interval is **288.71–422.04 K**. A state
outside a reaction law's measured range is calculated and marked, never excluded
because of its temperature. A native refusal remains explicit.

There are **278 fitted** and **452 not fitted** observations, in 22 groups.
The [role table](inputs/stage-b-data-roles.csv) retains each quantity, unit,
basis, temperature and source row. Earlier B1 model selection had already
accessed Xiao's 20 pressure observations and the primary 88-row Ermatchkov
comparison. All 101 Ermatchkov rows are now retained as not fitted: 88 at up to
49 wt% MDEA and 13 above that earlier comparison cutoff. This concentration
cutoff is separate from the reaction-temperature marks. Neither Xiao nor
Ermatchkov enters fitted-cost start selection. The inherited Xiao calculation
uses the declared bubble-pressure path; it does not explicitly model the
source's nitrogen carrier gas.

Start 0 ends on the native function tolerance:

from an endpoint and selects the lowest fitted cost, reporting ties within

The written, reloaded first endpoint gives cost **382.06387056091006**, a relative
native-cost difference of **4.3720582709738665e-13**. This is numerical replay
evidence, not a new fit or a physical validation statistic.

## Deviations, signed biases and reaction ranges

For an available prediction $m_i$ and observation $y_i$, the mean absolute
relative deviation is $100\langle |m_i-y_i|/|y_i|\rangle$ and signed relative bias
is $100\langle (m_i-y_i)/y_i\rangle$. Absolute error and signed error retain the
declared physical unit. Relative errors are undefined at either of the two
observed zeros; those observations remain in absolute errors and counts.
Counts below show available predictions / all observations in the marked set.

**273.15–498.15 K is the source-correlation range stated by Austgen 1991 Table V
p.547 (citing Edwards 1978), not verified measured coverage.** Every applicable
R1–R3 observation is inside that source-correlation range. MDEA dissociation
has measured range **278–368 K**. “Reaction not used” is distinct from “source
range unknown”; neither contributes to inside/outside totals. There are no
unknown-range marks in this MDEA declaration.

| Role | Inside MDEA range | Outside MDEA range | Reaction not used | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fitted | 161 | 32 | 85 | 278 |
| not fitted | 390 | 62 | 0 | 452 |
| All observations | 551 | 94 | 85 | 730 |

Among the **645** observations using MDEA dissociation, **85.426%** are inside
and **14.574%** outside its measured range. Over all 730 observations, the shares
are **75.479% inside**, **12.877% outside**, and **11.644% reaction not used**.
The shares describe declared rows, including unavailable calculations.

The following tables give every nonempty MDEA-range stratum for both models.
The [complete per-law comparison](results/stage-b-start-0-report/range-comparisons-with-b1.json)
retains all **188** nonempty model/group/law/range records and source-uncertainty
links. Each model's native `deviations.json` also preserves zero-count strata.
All 730 rows remain in each reduction; 717 predictions are available and 13
native refusals are retained.

## Source uncertainties and published model comparisons

The [source packet](inputs/stage-b-source-comparisons.json) retains exact PDF
identities, source locators, the 22 group mappings and measurement-uncertainty
statements. Current source PDFs were hash-checked against the retained source
identities. Parent verification corrects one Sobrino hash transcription in the
retrieved packet; the PDF and model inputs were unchanged. Residual scales
are fitting choices, not experimental uncertainty estimates. Published accuracy,
repeatability, standard uncertainty and expanded uncertainty are kept distinct.

| Stage B group(s) | Rows / role | Source uncertainty and applicability |
|---|---|---|
| `Bottinger-amine-sum-5bar`, `Bottinger-amine-sum-25bar`, `Bottinger-bicarbonate-5bar`, `Bottinger-bicarbonate-25bar` | 58 each / not fitted | Böttinger reports typical relative deviations below 3% for amine and below 5% for CO₂ mole fractions, with some CO₂ cases up to 10%; repeated peak-area fractions typically agree within 0.5%. These are accuracy/repeatability statements, not rowwise standard uncertainties. Table 2 has no per-row error bars. PDF p.3 / printed p.7919; Table 2 PDF p.6 / printed p.7922. |
| `Carson` | 40 / fitted | Carson estimates enthalpy measurement uncertainty at ±1–2% relative for the 298.15 K displacement-calorimetry results. The source does not identify this as a standard uncertainty or print rowwise uncertainties. Abstract; printed p.1294; Table 3 PDF p.9 / printed p.1293. |
| `Cp`, `Cp-60wt` | 33 fitted; 6 not fitted | Weiland reports heat-capacity repeatability of about 1% and standard-compound checks at about 1%. This is repeatability/reference-system evidence, not rowwise standard uncertainty. It applies to the 298.15 K heat-capacity measurements. Table 1 PDF p.1 / printed p.1004. |
| `Ermatchkov` | 101 / not fitted | For the 313.15, 353.15 and 393.15 K low-loading CO₂ partial pressures, Tables 1–3 print rowwise pressure uncertainty and CO₂-molality uncertainty. Pressure uncertainty is $\Delta p_{CO₂}=\pm(\Delta p^*_{CO₂}+0.02p_{CO₂})$: propagated T and molality effects through the paper’s VLE model plus calibration. Rowwise relative CO₂-molality uncertainty is about 0.1–3.9% (retained transcription range 0.08–3.95%). Table captions give ±0.1 K and ±0.1% MDEA molality. Each pressure point was repeated 3–8 times; the table separately prints repeatability standard deviation, which is not the measurement uncertainty. Tables 1–3, PDF pp.2–3 / printed pp.6082–6083. |
| `corrected-Kamps` | 28 / not fitted | Corrected Kamps total-pressure values in Ermatchkov Table 6 have no per-row uncertainty printed. The correction is a temperature recalibration described on printed pp.6085 and 6089; do not transfer the Table 1–3 low-loading uncertainty to this separate dataset. Table 6 PDF p.8 / printed p.6088. |
| `Jakobsen` | 16 / fitted | Jakobsen estimates NMR liquid-phase composition error at about 5–10%, largely temperature-dependent; very low species fractions may have higher errors. This is an approximate relative error range, not a standard uncertainty or per-row value. Table A5 PDF p.9 / printed p.9902; source statement in Abstract (PDF p.1) and Discussion. |
| `Kim` | 61 / fitted | Kim reports ±0.05 K temperature uncertainty and ±0.3 kPa pressure-controller uncertainty. The source describes less than 1% relative uncertainty across three parallel titrations of standard amine solutions; it does not assign that number as uncertainty to individual Table 8 equilibrium compositions. Table 8 PDF p.4 / printed p.2524; experimental/analytical discussion PDF p.6 / printed pp.2526–2527. |
| `Kuranov`, `Kuranov-413K` | 67 fitted; 13 not fitted | Kuranov reports ±0.1 K temperature uncertainty; pressure maximum uncertainty about 0.1% of the selected transducer’s full-scale range (0–0.6, 0–1.6, or 0–10 MPa); CO₂ weighing uncertainty ±0.008 g; MDEA concentration relative uncertainty below ±0.1%. Table 2 prints no rowwise pressure/loading uncertainties, and the paper does not map each row to a transducer range. Experimental Technique PDF p.3 / printed p.1959; Table 2. |
| `Merkley`, `Merkley-half-loading`, `Merkley-outside` | 4 fitted; 12 and 8 not fitted | Merkley estimates calorimetric heat accuracy at ±5%; five of 18 repeated systems agreed within 4%. These are accuracy and repeatability statements without rowwise uncertainties or coverage factor. The workflow’s ±0.02 mol/mol loading digitization uncertainty is a later transcription quantity, not the paper’s heat uncertainty. PDF p.3 / printed p.439; Figure 3 PDF p.5 / printed p.441. |
| `Sedighi` | 15 / not fitted | Sedighi reports no uncertainty for loading, pressure, temperature or composition. It reports ±0.1 mg balance accuracy for solvent preparation and triplicate averaging; neither is a propagated uncertainty for Table 3 loadings. Table 3 PDF p.8 / printed p.20; experimental procedure printed pp.15–17. |
| `Xiao` | 20 / not fitted | The Table 4 footnote states standard uncertainties: CO₂ pressure 1.5% relative, T 0.1 K, loading 0.004 mol CO₂/mol amine, unloaded MDEA 0.1 wt%, CO₂ 0.04 wt%, molality 0.01 mol/kg water. Common footnote values, not rowwise intervals. Applicability: 23.5 wt% unloaded MDEA, 298.15–313.15 K, 8.1–60.8 kPa CO₂ partial pressure, 0.101 MPa CO₂/N₂ total pressure. Table 4 and footnote PDF p.6 / printed p.175. |
| `Zheng` | 6 / not fitted | Table 4 gives standard $u(T)=0.01$ K and $u(P)=0.002$ MPa, plus relative expanded uncertainty 0.05 for saturated loading and heat. The coverage factor is not stated; common footnote values, not rowwise values. MDEA rows are at 323.15 K and 30 or 50 wt%. Table 4 footnote PDF p.5 / printed p.3788. |
| `loaded-density`, `density-60wt` | 33 fitted; 11 not fitted | Weiland 1998 says unloaded densities agreed with literature within 0.1%; that is a literature comparison, not an uncertainty for loaded density. No uncertainty for the carbonated-solution densities in Table 1 was found. Table 1 PDF p.2 / printed p.379; statement printed p.378. |
| `unloaded-density` | 24 / fitted | Sobrino Table 5 gives standard uncertainties $u(T)=0.01$ K, relative $u_r(p)=0.0001$, $u(w)=0.0001$ on mass fraction, and $u(\rho)=0.35$ kg/m³. The general density-meter statement is expanded uncertainty ($k=2$) below ±0.7 kg/m³. The table values are common source-level uncertainties, not per-row values. Table 5 footnote PDF p.4 / printed p.234; apparatus discussion PDF p.2. |


The residual tables place model errors beside these source statements without
assigning a confidence level the source does not supply. For example, the fitted
Kuranov pressure deviations are many percent, whereas its instrument statement
is 0.1% of full scale; the absent row-to-transducer mapping prevents a rowwise
relative-uncertainty test. Jakobsen's approximate 5–10% component-composition
error has not been propagated to this workflow's ratio observable. Neither
observation uncertainty propagation nor a statistical agreement test is claimed.
Ermatchkov's rowwise pressure uncertainty and separate repeatability columns
are retained at their source locators; they must not be interchanged.

## Parameter bounds and conditional standard errors

conditional-information calculation uses the real 278 fitted rows, their native
residual ordering and the declared residual model. Seven coordinates are free;
the MDEAH⁺–bicarbonate interaction is held at its active upper bound +1.
The residual variance is **2.81965956133513**. The calculation holds all shared
inputs, residual scales and that active bound fixed. It does not propagate
measurement uncertainty, shared-parameter uncertainty or model discrepancy.

## Unavailable predictions and the stability search

The first-endpoint and B1 reductions each retain 13 unavailable predictions.
The capped **288.71 K** state remains in the data and search set. Its native
prediction cause is `initial:thermochemistry_unavailable: outside_interval:
record excludes temperature`. Under #359 it is an unavailable search,
not a stable state; it is not dropped.

At **333.15 K, 60 wt% MDEA and 1.121 MPa**, the requested heat is unavailable.
For the first F2 endpoint the Engine reports `CentralSolveUnavailable`:

> saturation:loading 1.5: phase V has no locally unique anchored root: vapor branch not admitted by the finite search: the sole stable root 34728.073508897061 mol/m3 lies above the negative-slope sample 10734.505225582281 mol/m3;saturation:unexamined_gap;

This is a native finite-search refusal; no heat value or physical phase
conclusion is inferred. Both heat states and every other refused row retain
units, basis, source identity and their complete native messages in the data file.

The stability campaign uses MDEA's own **2,789** earlier native resolved-split
compositions, at every data state and the full **67-stock** grid. It never uses
the MEA split registry. The corrected historical inventory maps **13,582** native
witnesses, with **10,793** duplicate witnesses. All composition-bearing records
map; **620** scalar-only records cannot provide trial compositions and remain
excluded with provenance. Comparison-data role does not imply evaluation-only
mode. All **104** witness-source file hashes were verified before launch.
The [coverage](inputs/stage-b-registry-coverage.json) and compressed
[provenance](inputs/stage-b-registry-provenance.json.gz) retain those checks.

The grid spans 313.15–393.15 K in 10 K steps, 56 loadings from 1e-5 to the data
maximum 1.368 mol CO₂/mol MDEA, and 1.05 and 3.0 times each bubble pressure.
There are **67,536 grid entries**: **45,024** inside and **22,512** outside the
MDEA dissociation range, two thirds and one third respectively. These are
predeclared grid-entry counts, not completed or available search counts.
Supplied trials outside a state's fed/reacting component set will be counted
as not applicable, separately from unavailable evaluations. Evaluation-only
negative evidence will not be relabelled as a native resolved descent.

Search output is streamed to gzip with bounded work in flight on three
single-threaded workers under `agent-heavy`. The launch had 397,476,679,680 free
disk bytes, above the 85,899,345,920-byte two-search allowance with margin.
Runtime checkpoints identify their timing basis. No completed stability counts,
no-split conclusion or final split lower bound is yet available. If a search
finds a split, the campaign stops before penalties and reports witnesses and
elapsed times for the owner's decision. No penalty stage is authorized here.
